text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 3.6% today, climbing to $410.84, as oil prices stabilized following news that a damaged Saudi Arabian pipeline will restart operations within days. The closure had briefly pushed U.S. crude above $105 per barrel earlier in the week, but today's announcement of the pipeline's imminent return eased supply concerns—U.S. oil is now trading at $97.26, down from those highs. Refineries are running at 97.8% capacity with healthy product inventories, positioning the company to benefit from the current crude environment without acute supply disruptions.

This move fits a broader week of volatility tied to Middle Eastern tensions. Earlier this week, Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure had spiked prices and raised geopolitical risk premiums; today's pipeline restart signal suggests those supply fears are receding, which typically pressures oil prices but can actually improve refiner margins by lowering their crude input costs while refined product demand remains stable.
